title: Canonical ordinary pro-etale projective-line comparison and trace arrows
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring in universe $u+1$, and use schemes in universe $u$ and ordinary constant-ring module derived categories on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], [sk-def-sfb-finite-derived-functors]. Write $\nu_T^*$ for the exact termwise etale-to-pro-etale comparison [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback], and use the etale constant objects, inverse images and derived direct images of [def-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-arrows]. Define $C_T=\nu_T^*$ on ordinary unbounded derived categories, $f^*=L(f^{-1})$, and $Rf_*=R(f_*)$. Define the pull comparison $f^*C_Y\cong C_X f^{-1}$ by the actual site-comparison square; the push comparison $C_YRf_*K\to Rf_*C_XK$ is its adjunction mate, namely the adjunct of pull comparison followed by the image of the etale counit. Define the sum comparison $C_TK\oplus C_TL\to C_T(K\oplus L)$ by the two images of the injections. For $N\in\mathbf N$ with $NA=0$, put $U_T=C_T(A_{T,et})$ and $A_T(a)[b]=C_T(A_{T,et}(a)[b])$ for $a,b\in\mathbf Z$, using the signed shifted twists of [def-sp-p1-decomposition-arrows]. Define $f^*U_Y\cong U_X$ by pull comparison followed by constant pullback. When $N>0$ is invertible on $Y$, define $f^*A_Y(a)[b]\cong A_X(a)[b]$ by pull comparison and the roots-normalized signed-twist pullback [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Put $q_T:P_T=\mathbf P^1_T\to T$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. For every $g:T'\to T$, define the source comparison on $U_T\oplus A_T(-1)[-2]$ by its two projections followed by constant and twist pullback; define projective-line exchange to be the adjunction mate for its Cartesian base-change square [def-kun-unbounded-exchange]. Its unit and positive-twist versions are exchange followed by $Rq_{T',*}$ of the corresponding coefficient pullback. Finally, for any specified isomorphism $b:A_T(1)[2]\oplus U_T\cong Rq_{T,*}A_{P_T}(1)[2]$, define its trace to be $b^{-1}$ followed by the second projection. These are definitions only: no invertibility of decomposition or exchange is asserted, and no Noetherian or flatness hypothesis is imposed.
